item.title: Carrick driving instructor highlights importance of road safety
item.description: A Carrickmacross driving instructor has highlighted the importance of road safety. Claire McEneaney from Claire's School of Motoring is an RSA approved driving instructor based in Carrickmacross and Dundalk. Claire warned that in her opinion, roads have become "so dangerous" adding that 2025 was a heart-breaking year on Irish roads where 185 lives were lost, the highest since 2014. item.title: Mother of young woman found dead in Monaghan issues appeal
item.description: The mother of a 23 year old woman who was found dead in Monaghan 100 weeks ago has appealed for information. Kelly Lynch was discovered in the Ulster Canal in Monaghan town on St Patrick's Day 2024. Gardaí believe she wandered off alone and fell from a bridge into the canal and are not treating her death as suspicious. item.title: No stopping Shane on his latest world record
item.description: Clones man Shane McLaughlin broke his sixth world record over the weekend as he pulled a 120 tonne boat over five metres. The 54-year-old Paralympian and amputee, completed the feat at Rossaveel Harbour in Connemara when he pulled Aran Island Ferries’ largest vessel, Saoirse na Farraige. The vessel is the largest passenger-only ferry registered in Irish waters. item.title: Ballyjamesduff man creates app predicting the Northern Lights
item.description: A Ballyjamesduff man has created an app that will predict when the Northern Lights will occur. The application that Aaron Kelly has developed was published on the play store in recent weeks. The idea behind the app is targeted at basic and advanced users to help predict Aurora. Northern Lights Alerts is a data driven Northern Lights forecasting tool. According to Aaron the aim of the app is to inform people of what to expect and when to expect it. item.title: Jury sworn in for the murder trial of Natalie McNally
item.description: A jury's been sworn in to serve in the trial of a man accused of the murder of Natalie McNally. A jury of six men and six women were sworn in to serve during the trial. They were urged to decide the case on the evidence that they heard in court, and not to do their own research. The 32-year old was 15 weeks pregnant when she was killed at her Lurgan home in December 2022. 35-year old Stephen McCullagh from Lisburn's Woodland Gardens has denied murdering her. Advertisement

item.title: Hive of Knowledge will relocate to Monaghan Peace Campus
item.description: The Hive of Knowledge sculpture will be relocated to the Peace Campus on Glaslough Street, with the structure expected to be in place within approximately six weeks. The news was confirmed to Northern Sound by Fine Gael's Pauric Clerkin. Cllr Clerkin said this development represents a major step forward following his sustained campaign to have the Hive of Knowledge removed from storage and returned to public view in Monaghan Town. item.description: Children preparing for their confirmation will be asked to make a commitment not to vape before they're 18. The Confirmation Pledge has been updated to include vapes and cigarettes. The promise not to use e-cigarettes will be added to abstaining from drinking alcohol or doing drugs. item.title: Clones Bikers' memorial site beside marina shelved
item.description: Monaghan County Council have confirmed following a presentation today on the public consultation and survey for the proposed National Bikers Memorial in Clones, elected members have decided not to proceed with Páirc Phobail Séamus Mac Cába as a location. The local authority said there is strong support locally for a memorial, and Monaghan County Council will continue working with the Gone but Not Forgotten Committee to find a suitable alternative site in Clones.
